# Template demonstration {#sec-template-demo}

This chapter is a functional check of the template. Its example is deliberately elementary so that the focus remains on authoring and layout conventions.

:::: {.concept-layout}
::: {.concept-main}
## Mathematical content

::: {#def-parameterized-function name="Parameterized function"}
A **parameterized function** is a family of functions whose behavior depends on one or more explicitly identified parameters. The parameter is held fixed when the function is evaluated with respect to its input.
:::

For a minimal example of @def-parameterized-function, consider

$$
f(x;a) = a x^2.
$$ {#eq-demo-function}

In @eq-demo-function, $x$ is the input and $a$ is a parameter. Its sign controls whether the curve opens upward or downward, while its magnitude controls the vertical scale. This statement is the complete mathematical point of the example; the panel only makes the relationship easier to inspect.

The graph in @fig-demo-curve responds to the slider. It is produced by a local Observable JS cell, while the small renderer lives separately under `widgets/demo/`. This separation follows the broader literate-programming idea that exposition and computation should support one another [@knuth1984literate].

## Reuse this pattern

Copy the semantic structure of this section when an explanation benefits from a companion visualization. Keep the `.concept-main` block self-contained, place optional controls in `.interactive-panel`, and give any plot a `fig-` label and caption so it can be referenced from the text.
:::

::: {.interactive-panel aria-labelledby="interactive-heading"}
## Explore the parameter {#interactive-heading}

Move the slider to change $a$ in @eq-demo-function. The axes remain fixed so that changes of sign and scale are directly comparable.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import { renderLineChart } from "../widgets/demo/widget.js"
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof a = Inputs.range([-2, 2], {
  label: "Coefficient a",
  value: 1,
  step: 0.1
})
```

```{ojs}
//| label: fig-demo-curve
//| fig-cap: "The graph of $f(x;a)=ax^2$ for the selected value of $a$."
//| echo: false
renderLineChart({
  points: Array.from({ length: 161 }, (_, index) => {
    const x = -2 + index / 40;
    return { x, y: a * x * x };
  }),
  xDomain: [-2, 2],
  yDomain: [-8, 8],
  xLabel: "x",
  yLabel: "f(x; a)",
  accessibleLabel: `Graph of f(x; a) = a x squared with a = ${a.toFixed(1)}`
})
```

The panel is sticky on wider screens and moves below the main text on smaller screens. No server or framework is required.
:::
